ing: finely chopped, plus more raw to serve
st: Put the beef, pork, garlic, paprika, baking soda, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the sparkling water and knead the meat firmly by hand for 8 minutes until it is sticky and holds together.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour; overnight is better.
With wet hands, shape the meat into small fingers about 3 inches long and 3/4 inch thick, about 24 in all.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high.
Grill the ćevapi for 10 to 12 minutes, turning often, until browned and at least 160°F (71°C) inside.
Warm the flatbread on the grill for 30 seconds per side.
Serve 4 ćevapi per flatbread with chopped raw onion and kajmak on the side.

ing: grated, plus raw slices to serve
st: Combine the beef, pork, grated onion, garlic, paprika, pepper and salt in a large bowl.
Add the sparkling water and mix by hand for 5 minutes until the mixture feels sticky.
Cover and chill the meat for 30 minutes.
Divide into 4 portions and shape each into a flat patty about 6 inches wide and 3/4 inch thick. Press a shallow dimple in the middle.
Heat a grill or heavy skillet to medium-high and brush with the oil.
Cook the patties for 5 to 6 minutes per side until browned and at least 160°F (71°C) in the center.
Warm the flatbread, place a patty inside, and top with kajmak and onion slices. Serve at once.
Heat the oil and cook the onions and chopped bacon for 8 minutes. Stir in the paprika for 30 seconds and cool.
In a large bowl mix the pork, beef, rice, the onion mixture, pepper and salt.
Trim the thick ribs from the cabbage leaves. Put about [[3 tbsp]] filling on each leaf, fold the sides in, and roll tightly.
Spread the shredded sauerkraut and 2 bacon slices on the bottom of a heavy pot. Pack in the rolls snugly in layers, adding the bay leaves and other bacon slices between layers.
Pour in [[3 cups]] water to nearly cover the rolls and put a plate on top to hold them down.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on very low heat for 2 hours 30 minutes, until the cabbage is soft and the meat reaches 160°F (71°C).
Rest for 15 minutes, then serve with sour cream and bread.

ing: or mascarpone and a little cream cheese
st: Slice each cutlet so you can open it flat, then pound to about 1/4 inch thick between plastic wrap.
Season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Spoon a quarter of the kajmak on one half of each cutlet, then roll up and tuck in the sides so it is a tight cylinder. Secure with toothpicks.
Chill the rolls for 20 minutes to firm up.
Coat each roll in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing so they stick. For extra crunch, dip in egg and crumbs a second time.
Heat the oil to 340°F (170°C) in a deep skillet. Fry the rolls 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and check that the pork reaches 145°F (63°C). Remove toothpicks.
Serve sliced with lemon wedges, tartar sauce, and fries.
Soak the beans in cold water overnight, then drain.
Put the beans in a pot with fresh cold water to cover, boil hard for 10 minutes, and drain. This makes the beans easier to digest.
Return the beans to the pot with the smoked ribs, bay leaves and [[8 cups]] fresh water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer, partly covered, for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Meanwhile cook the onions and carrots in the oil for 10 minutes until golden. Stir in the flour, then the paprika and garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir this mixture into the pot with the salt and pepper and simmer for 30 minutes more until the beans are very soft and the broth is thick.
Taste and adjust the salt. Remove the bay leaves, and serve with bread and pickled peppers.

ing: large, such as gigante or lima, soaked overnight
st: Soak the beans overnight in cold water, then drain. Cover with fresh water in a pot and boil for 10 minutes.
Add the bay leaves and simmer for about 45 minutes until the beans are tender but still whole. Drain, keeping [[1 cup]] of the cooking water.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). In a skillet cook the onions in the oil over medium-low heat for 20 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, paprika, hot paprika, salt and pepper and stir for 1 minute.
Mix the beans with the onion mixture and the reserved water and spread them in a baking dish.
Bake uncovered for 45 minutes until the top is browned and slightly crisp and the beans are creamy.
Cool for 10 minutes. Serve warm or at room temperature.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Brush a 9x13-inch baking dish with the oil.
Mash the feta in a bowl and whisk in the eggs, yogurt, sparkling water and salt to make a lumpy filling.
Lay 3 phyllo sheets in the dish, brushing each with melted butter. Spread with a thin layer of filling.
Repeat, 2 sheets then filling, until the filling is used, keeping the sheets covered with a damp towel so they do not dry out.
Finish with 3 buttered phyllo sheets on top and brush with the remaining butter. Cut into squares with a sharp knife before baking.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until deep golden and puffed and the center is set.
Rest for 15 minutes before serving.

Cook the onion in [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet for 6 minutes. Add the beef, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, breaking it up, until fully cooked through to 160°F (71°C). Cool.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Mix [[0.5 cup]] oil with the sparkling water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt for brushing.
Lay one phyllo sheet on the counter and brush with the oil mix. Spoon a line of filling along the long edge.
Roll the dough up into a long thin rope and coil it into a spiral in an oiled round 10-inch pan.
Repeat with the remaining sheets and filling, coiling each rope against the last to fill the pan.
Brush the top with the remaining oil mix and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Rest for 10 minutes and cut into wedges. Serve with yogurt.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush a 9x13-inch baking dish with [[1 tbsp]] oil and put it in the oven for 5 minutes.
Mix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl whisk the eggs, yogurt, [[0.33 cup]] oil and warm water until smooth.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry and stir until just combined, then fold in the feta.
Pour the batter into the hot pan; it will sizzle at the edges.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool for 10 minutes, then cut into squares and serve warm.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Roast the whole peppers and eggplant on lined sheet pans for 40 to 50 minutes, turning, until the skins are blistered and black.
Put the hot vegetables in a covered bowl for 15 minutes to steam, which loosens the skins.
Peel the peppers and remove the seeds and stems. Peel the eggplant and drain off bitter juices.
Chop everything finely, or pulse in a food processor for a thick, slightly rough paste.
Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pot and add the vegetable paste. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for 40 minutes until thick and dark.
Stir in the garlic, vinegar, salt and sugar and cook 5 more minutes.
Cool, then store in clean jars in the fridge for up to 2 weeks. Serve with bread or grilled meat.
Put the feta in a bowl and mash it with a fork until crumbly and mostly smooth.
Add the sour cream and whip with the fork or a hand mixer for 1 to 2 minutes until fluffy.
Stir in the minced chili, garlic and paprika.
Beat in the oil a little at a time until the spread is creamy.
Taste. Feta is salty so you probably do not need extra salt. Add more chili for a hotter spread.
Chill for 15 minutes so the flavors blend, then top with parsley and a dusting of paprika.
